events.continuity_hook: Keep the Friday-to-Monday dates, two travelers, Saturday 6:30 p.m. Point Loma dinner, and Sunday afternoon Balboa Park gathering fixed while selecting the flights.
events.interaction_goal: Compare total airfare for two, airport transfer timing, Friday check-in practicality, and the usable time created by each Monday return, then choose both flights and fix the hotel-night count.
events.scenario_brief: Elena and her spouse are comparing two Friday nonstops from Denver: an earlier arrival that leaves time to check in and meet relatives for an informal meal, and a lower-fare evening arrival that reaches San Diego after the hotel’s dining service ends. Monday options are a late-morning nonstop or an early-evening departure that preserves most of the day but requires luggage storage and adds a higher fare for two travelers.

events.continuity_hook: Use the confirmed flights, three-night shared stay, offered Saturday ride, Sunday Balboa Park gathering, and need for Monday luggage storage.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate complete lodging and local transportation totals, verify cancellation and luggage-storage terms, choose the more practical property, and prepare the reservation for two adults.
events.scenario_brief: The couple has selected a Friday afternoon arrival and Monday early-evening return, so they need one room for three nights plus luggage storage after checkout. The waterfront hotel is closer to Saturday’s dinner but lists a parking charge and destination fee separately, while the central property has a higher room rate, lower transportation estimates for Sunday and Monday, and a different cancellation deadline. Relatives have offered rides for the Saturday dinner but not for the Sunday gathering.

events.continuity_hook: Complete the existing family weekend using the chosen central hotel, confirmed Friday and Monday flights, and one shared room for three nights.
events.interaction_goal: Correct the occupancy to two adults, check the final charges and local-time cancellation cutoff, confirm Monday bag storage, and assemble the completed trip details.
events.scenario_brief: Elena is ready to reserve the selected central San Diego hotel for herself and her spouse. The checkout page reflects the expected three-night total, but the room occupancy defaults to one adult, and the listed cancellation cutoff uses the hotel’s local time. Their Monday flight departs well after checkout, so the confirmation also needs a clear note about holding two bags that afternoon.

events.continuity_hook: Open a new solo professional trip that reaches downtown Providence before Thursday’s committee dinner and continues through Saturday’s author breakfast.
events.interaction_goal: Develop workable flight and hotel combinations, account for the ground trip from the available arrival airports, and identify which Thursday arrival and Saturday return pairings leave adequate margins around the scheduled events.
events.scenario_brief: Elena is planning a solo trip from Denver to Providence for a university-press board meeting. A committee dinner begins Thursday at 6:00 p.m., board sessions occupy Friday from 8:30 a.m. through 5:00 p.m., and an author breakfast ends Saturday at 10:00 a.m. She can return Saturday, and the meeting hotel is downtown, while a less expensive property near the train station would add a walk or short ride to each scheduled event.

events.continuity_hook: Keep the Thursday committee dinner, full Friday board schedule, Saturday 10:00 a.m. breakfast finish, and solo itinerary fixed while choosing the airports and flights.
events.interaction_goal: Compare complete fares, connection exposure, airport-to-downtown travel, and event margins, then select the outbound and return and establish the lodging dates.
events.scenario_brief: No suitable nonstop serves the full route. Elena can connect through Chicago and reach Providence in midafternoon Thursday, leaving a moderate margin before the 6:00 p.m. dinner, or take an earlier itinerary into Boston and continue by ground transportation with more transfer complexity. Saturday choices include a Providence departure shortly after the author breakfast or a later Boston departure that allows a wider margin but requires a timed rail or car transfer.

events.continuity_hook: Use the confirmed Thursday arrival, Saturday Boston departure, two solo nights, and all events at the downtown meeting hotel.
events.interaction_goal: Normalize the two-night totals, include local travel and breakfast costs, verify payment, cancellation, and luggage-hold terms, then choose and reserve the hotel while preserving enough time for the Saturday airport transfer.
events.scenario_brief: Elena has chosen the Thursday itinerary into Providence and a later Saturday departure from Boston, fixing a two-night stay and a post-breakfast transfer. The downtown meeting hotel costs more but keeps the dinner, Friday sessions, and breakfast in one building; the station-area hotel is cheaper before taxes but charges for breakfast and has a stricter prepaid rate. Both can hold luggage Saturday, though only one states that service clearly in the rate terms.
